findings.title: Recursive non-void function that can fall off its end emits `return __extc_ret_v;` for an undeclared variable (generated C does not compile)
findings.why: The guard is exactly the broken case. `__extc_ret_v` is declared only when `bool retSlot = !g->noArena && !retVoid;` (line 4868-4870). This branch runs only when `g->noArena` is true and `retVoid` is false, i.e. precisely when retSlot was false and the slot was never declared, so the emitted C names an undeclared identifier. The comment claims the `fallsOff` guard avoids the problem, but `fallsOff` is what reaches it; the real fix is to not emit the return (the trap emitted just below, line 4969-4979, is the correct behaviour and is even left as dead code after it).
findings.trigger: Any self-recursive (directly or transitively, per funcCallsItself) non-void function whose body does not end in a definite `return` and which uses no block arena (`mayUseArena` false, no @overwrite site): `fn f(n: i64) -> i64 { if n > 0 { return f(n - 1) } }`.

findings.title: Coroutine declared as a method references `struct <owner>_<name>$frame` while the frame struct is named `<name>$frame` and is never defined
findings.why: Every frame reference in codegen is built from `cFuncName(g, coroOf)`, which for a method is `<owner>_<name>` (line 653-654), and cType() does the same (line 486). The frame StructDef, however, is created by the checker with `frameOwner = f->instName ? f->instName : f->name` (src/check_top.c:3962-3964), i.e. the bare method name, and is emitted through the type channel under that name. The two names can never be reconciled for a method, so the emitted unit uses an undefined struct type and the frame struct itself is never defined.
findings.trigger: A coroutine function declared inside a struct/impl block (a method), e.g. `impl tick { fn count(self: ref tick) -> coroutine<i64> { ... } }`, driven from main.

findings.title: A boxed instance of a generic coroutine never ends its task: the frame's task arena and zone are leaked and the dead-handle trap can never fire
findings.code_quote:
cgLine(g, "    case %d: return %s%s((struct %s$frame *)h->frame);",
               cf->coroKind, cn, cf->coroNeedsZone ? "$next" : "$step", cn);
...
        if (!__r) extc_task_end(f->task);   /* ran to completion: same release as a drop */
findings.why: `extc_task_end` is called from exactly one place, the `$next` driver emitted in genCoroDecls (line 4613), and that loop skips every instance (`if (!f || !f->isCoro || f->tmpl || f->typeParams.len > 0) continue;` line 4600). Whether the dispatch uses `$next` or `$step` is `coroNeedsZone`, which the checker computes only for non-instances (`if (!cf || !cf->isCoro || cf->tmpl) continue;` src/check_top.c:6570), so a generic coroutine instance that is boxed (coroBoxed true, hence a handle and a task frame) still has coroNeedsZone == false. The handle dispatch then calls `$step` directly, `extc_task_end` is never reached, and the task's arena (`extc_taskArena[id]`, which owns the frame) and the zone pushed by the spawn are never released; `extc_task_alive(id)` also stays 1 forever, so driving a handle past completion cannot trap as the generated comment (line 4486-4488) promises.
findings.trigger: Any `var h: coroutine<T> = gen(...)` where `gen` is a *generic* coroutine (`fn gen<T>(x: T) -> coroutine<T>`), driven to completion, especially in a loop.

findings.title: A coroutine body that needs hidden frame state emits `__extc_a[1]` / `__extc_home`, neither of which exists in a step function (dead @overwrite cell, and calls through the hidden home arena)
findings.why: For a step function `g->noArena` is forced true (line 4744), so the `extc_arena __extc_a[]` array is never declared, and the hidden `__extc_home` parameter is declared only for `main` (line 4877). But the @overwrite prologue still emits one cell per site, initialised with `&__extc_a[1]` or `__extc_home`, inside `$step`. Worse, the cell is *dead*: the coroutine `var` path (line 3874-3882) returns before the @overwrite lowering at line 3893, so the site allocates normally and `__extc_ow0` is never read (a warning-level unused local, with -Werror an error by itself). The same undeclared-`__extc_home` breakage happens with no @overwrite at all, whenever the body calls a function that takes the hidden home arena.
findings.trigger: Trigger A: any `@overwrite var x = new ...` inside a coroutine body. Trigger B: a coroutine whose body calls a function that takes a hidden home arena, e.g. `yield i64(mk(i64(9))[0])` with `fn mk(n: i64) -> slice<i64> { var p = new [4]i64  return p[0..4] }`.

findings.title: Coroutine handle helpers embed the yield type's C spelling in an identifier: a `ref` yield type emits `extc_coro_value_int64_t *` and the call site parses as a multiplication
findings.why: `yt = cType(g, cf->yieldType)` is used as part of a C *identifier*, but cType returns arbitrary C type syntax: a pointer type becomes `int64_t *` (cType, line 475 `case TY_REF: return arenaPrintf(g->arena, "%s *", ...)`). The emitted helper is then syntactically invalid, and the call site (line 770 of the generated file) becomes `s = (s + ((int64_t)((*(extc_coro_value_int64_t *(&h, "t2.extc", 9))))));` -- a multiplication by an undeclared identifier. Nothing restricts coroutine yield types to name-shaped types, and the checker accepts the program.
findings.trigger: Any coroutine whose yield type is not a valid C identifier fragment but whose handle is created (boxed), e.g. `fn g(x: ref i64) -> coroutine<ref i64>` plus `var h: coroutine<ref i64> = g(ref v)`.

findings.title: Recursive coroutine increments the recursion guard but never decrements it: sequential spawns eventually die with a bogus `recursion too deep` trap
findings.why: The coroutine step is emitted through the same prologue as an ordinary function, so a (transitively) self-recursive coroutine gets `extc_rec_enter`, but the coroutine branch returns before the epilogue where `cgRecLeave` is emitted, and a resume jumps past `extc_rec_enter` anyway. The depth counter is therefore monotonic: one increment per *created* coroutine, no decrement ever (grep of the generated file finds `extc_rec_enter` once and no `--__extc_rec_depth` outside the runtime). After EXTC_REC_LIMIT (100000) spawns the guard traps although the program's real recursion depth is O(1).
findings.trigger: A coroutine that is (transitively) self-recursive and is created more than 100000 times in sequence; e.g. `rec` yields and calls an ordinary `drive`, which creates another `rec` frame.

findings.title: Exponential compile time in block-depth computation: blkMaxOfBlock evaluates blkMaxLevel twice per statement, so nesting depth d costs 2^d
findings.why: The recursive walk is duplicated per child (the second call re-does the whole subtree instead of reusing the first result), and blkMaxLevel for a block calls blkMaxOfBlock again, so T(d) = 2*T(d-1) + O(1): compile time doubles per nesting level instead of being linear in the AST. My range's genFunc calls it once per function (`int maxLv = 1 + blkMaxOfBlock(f->body);`, line 4715) and cgCoroArenaDestroy calls it per coroutine (line 3403), so every function pays it. Perf sampling confirms it: on 32 nested blocks `perf` puts 45% in blkMaxOfBlock and 41% in blkMaxLevel (85% total).
findings.trigger: A function body with d nested blocks (`{ { { ... } } }`, machine-generated code or deeply nested scopes). Also any nesting through if/while/match bodies.
findings.repro:
for n in 24 26 28 30 32: generate `fn f() -> i64 { var x: i64 = 0` + n times `{ x = x + 1` + n closing braces + `return x }` + main, then time ./build/extc f.extc -o f.c:
  n=24 0.15 s, n=26 0.60 s, n=28 2.30 s, n=30 9.21 s, n=32 36.94 s  (x4 per +2 levels)
  n=70 never finished (killed after 60 s); generated C size stays linear (10 KB at n=28), so this is pure compiler blowup.
expected: linear-ish in the AST; the duplicated call is the whole difference.

findings.title: Pool-owning coroutine driven as a stack frame leaks its whole place: the spawn restores extc_zoneTop before the task ends, so extc_task_end's zoneLeaveTo(task zone) is a no-op
findings.why: For a stack frame (`var c = f(...)`, not a handle) with `cf->coroNeedsZone`, the spawn stores `.zone = extc_task_zone(id)` in the frame and immediately restores `extc_zoneTop` to the caller's depth (line 3841). When the coroutine later finishes, `$next` restores `extc_zoneTop = __sv` (the caller's depth, which is task_zone - 1) *before* calling `extc_task_end`; extc_task_end does `extc_pool_zoneLeaveTo(extc_taskZone[id])`, whose loop is `while (extc_zoneTop >= mark && extc_zoneTop >= 0)`. With zoneTop < mark the loop never runs, so the task's pools are not dropped, the orphaned zone entry (id = caller_depth+1) keeps its pool chain, and the pool/plate memory survives. The bundled tests only drive one such coroutine once (tests/coro/coro_pool.extc, run.sh:314), which is exactly the case that hides it. Reproduced: RSS grows by ~5 KB per spawn (the pool's exact size) while the boxed path that keeps the task zone current stays flat at ~14 MB, so the no-op leave is the leak.
findings.trigger: A stack-frame coroutine that creates a pool (hence coroNeedsZone) and is spawned repeatedly in a loop, e.g. `while k < N { var c = g(i64(1))  while c.next() { }  k = k + 1 }` with `g` building a `vector<T>::withCap(...)`.

coverage_notes:
Read codegen.c 4301-6450 completely in ~650-line chunks (plus the surrounding callers/callees needed to judge them: CG struct comments 90-350, cgCoroArenaDestroy 3400-3410, blkMaxLevel/blkMaxOfBlock 3615-3667, genBlockBody 3680-3715, the @overwrite lowering 3888-4000, coroutine frame/boxing emission 2100-2160 and 2363-2404, g.funcs construction 6975-7040, the emission loop 8213-8235 and the final assembly/splice order 8455-8578). Functions in range examined line by line: stmtIsDefiniteReturn, the FuncSet/cycDfs/cycleSaysRecursive cycle analysis (linear probing is safe: funcSetAdd grows at load 0.5, and g_cyc* globals are only reused if generateC ran twice, which main.c:528 never does), coroProvisional/coroEmitted, genCoroHandleDecls, genCoroDecls, the cg-time/str/loc counters, genFunc (prologue, main(args) view, @overwrite cells, ret slot, recursion guard, coro Duff's-device step and its early return, arena/zone release loop, fallsOff and the non-void trap, epilogue restores), cgIsMain, genFuncProto, globalFnProto, the SUnit/unitFind/unitBody dependency ordering and @frozen _Static_asserts, sliceHelper/genSlice (bounds go through extc_checkedRange(lo,hi,n) 
with 0<=lo<=hi<=n and the literal fast path is guarded by the checker's proved-range errors - verified with out-of-range literal slices being rejected), addInstanceUnit/scanTypeForUnits/scanUnitForUnits, funcSignatureMentionsParam, countMentions/countMentionsIn/countCodeMentions/countReads (literal+comment skipping is parity-sensitive but the only emitted in-body comment with an apostrophe, line 4879, sits in main's prologue before mainBody, so countReads' region never sees it today), localDef, deadFuncBody, macroDefineName, dropRuntimeDefs (span/brace pairing and the memmove length guard look correct; total/inside counting errs toward keeping), dropUnusedLocals (cut assembly is ordered, shadowed locals get distinct cnames, traps inside discarded RHS expressions survive because they lower to helper calls; the `(void)(%s);` rewrite would mis-handle a trailing comment on a rewritten declaration line, but no generated declaration line carries one), dropUnreferenced and ensureUnusedMacro. Verified-correct-by-construction: par trampoline nViews>=1 is enforced by the checker (check_expr.c:2031-2050, params.len>=4 and exactly one mut view), loopLevel[64] overflow is unreachable because genBlockBody's assert fires first, and 64-deep nesting cannot be reached anyway because of the exponential blkMax blowup above. All eight findings were reproduced with /tmp scratch files (for the zone/pool one: /tmp/zl.extc 263 MB vs the 1-element and boxed-handle controls 21 MB / 14 MB) and ./build/extc (--check-c / --run / patched generated C for the extc_task_live probe).
